posts.theme: University of Illinois Marching Illini packed Times Square after the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed, then stayed to march
posts.quote: Illinois Marching Band Packed Times Square After New York Postponed The 100th Thanksgiving Parade
posts.alt: Photo of the University of Illinois Marching Illini in navy and orange dress uniforms marching in a city street parade in 2014, with a bass drum labeled University of Illinois Marching Illini. This is not a photo of the November 2026 Times Square pep rally. Headline text at the bottom: Illinois Marching Band Packed Times Square After New York Postponed The 100th Thanksgiving Parade. Break The Spin logo top left. Photo credit: Miguel Mendez, CC BY 2.0.
posts.caption:
New York postponed the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. First time in the parade's history. A coastal storm was coming in, with forecast winds high enough to ground the balloons. Bands from across the country had already spent a fortune to get there.

The University of Illinois Marching Illini did not go home.

That night, more than 400 students packed Times Square with a full pep rally. A packed crowd. Illinois fans. Alumni who live in the city. Senior Taylor Herman said, "We could hear the echoes off the buildings." This was not a protest. It was a college marching band that came to play in the most famous parade in America. When the parade got postponed, they filled the most famous intersection in America instead.

Then they stayed.

Band director Barry Houser told the students they were marching when the parade was rescheduled for November 28. The extra hotels, buses, and meals were estimated at $175,000, on top of a trip that had already cost about $600,000. Students had paid $275 apiece. Parade organizers had not offered to cover the added cost. So the band asked Illini Nation for help. The money came in.

The University of Alabama's band packed up and left. Illinois stayed. Connecticut stayed too.

These kids were one of only 10 bands chosen for the 100th parade. It was their second trip, after 2015. Houser compared it to a national championship, the grandest stage there is for a marching band.

Sorry but this is what it looks like when Midwestern college students refuse to quit. New York postponed a tradition because of the weather. Fair enough. The Marching Illini packed Times Square, raised the money, and waited to march anyway.
posts.first:
The facts: The University of Illinois Marching Illini held a pep rally in Times Square on the night of November 25, 2026, hours after Macy's postponed the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade from November 26 to November 28 because of a coastal storm, the first postponement in the parade's history. The band has about 410 members and was one of 10 selected from more than 100 applicants. The pep rally had been planned and was set to air on Inside Edition. On November 26, director Barry Houser announced the band would stay. Extra costs were estimated at $175,000 on top of a trip already estimated at $600,000. The University of Alabama dropped out. The University of Connecticut stayed. Senior Ryan Hanson said, "It was really cool to see how many people were there to support us, and how many Illinois fans were here, including alumni who were based in New York." Announcing the postponement with Macy's and the NYPD, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said, "I know that this change of plans will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first."

Sources: CBS Chicago, Nov. 26, 2026; NBC Chicago, Nov. 25, 2026; Chicago Sun-Times, Nov. 26, 2026; Daily Herald, Nov. 26, 2026; Smile Politely, Nov. 25, 2026; NYC Mayor's Office transcript, Nov. 25, 2026.
